text.p: Interline Resources Corp said Tuesday that it was unable to pay about $2.2 million owed to Genesis Petroleum Inc on October 17, 1996, as required by a June 19, 1996 agreement between the companies.
Interline also said that it was unable to repay loans totaling about $2.5 million from an individual lender, and loans from this person are currently in default.
Under the agreement with Genesis, Interline was to make this payment in exchange for Genesis' interest in an oil reprocessing plant in Salt Lake City.
Interline said it is engaged in discussions with Genesis regarding a possible resolution of the situation, but there can be no assurance that any agreement will be reached.

Interline said lender of the $2.5 million has indicated that he does not currently intend to take remedial action against Interline, and the company is attempting to renegotiate the terms of these loans.
The loans are secured by the assets of the company.
